chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant on neuroblastoma
predictions: The variant has no reproducible allele-dependent TF-mediated effect on enhancer output or LMO1 regulation in neuroblastoma cells.
Any apparent neuroblastoma relevance is not caused by this variant's TF-mediated effect; the variant's other-trait associations do not establish a neuroblastoma mechanism.
falsified_if: Allele-specific binding and TF-specific perturbation show that this base reproducibly changes enhancer output and alters LMO1 regulation in neuroblastoma cells.

chains.title: Reduced GATA2 binding alters a candidate LMO1 enhancer

links.claim: GATA2 is occupied over the variant and highly expressed in SK-N-SH; its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger binding to ref C than alt A. GATA3 is also occupied and has independent support for the same direction, so GATA2 is a well-supported candidate, not uniquely identified as the responsible GATA factor.
The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1518342, but the reported activity scores are maxima across biosamples and do not establish activity in SK-N-SH.

LMO1 is a plausible target because the variant is intronic to LMO1, the cCRE lists LMO1 among nearby genes, and gene prioritization favors LMO1; these data do not show that this cCRE regulates LMO1 in SK-N-SH.
GATA2 occupancy and high expression are reported in SK-N-SH, making this a plausible context for a GATA2 binding effect.
An effect on LMO1 could be relevant to neuroblastoma biology, but the supplied evidence does not connect this variant or its proposed GATA2 mechanism to neuroblastoma risk.

predictions: If the variant changes GATA2 binding in SK-N-SH, allele-specific occupancy should favor C over A.
A GATA2-specific perturbation should affect any C-versus-A difference in enhancer output more than a GATA3-specific perturbation; the direction of an LMO1 expression effect is not established.
falsified_if: A sensitive allele-specific assay finds no C-over-A GATA2 occupancy difference in SK-N-SH.
GATA2-specific perturbation leaves a reproducible variant-dependent enhancer effect unchanged, while GATA3-specific perturbation removes it.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr11:8233861:C>A, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000149), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 12 occupied (5 with a strong site), 5 of 115 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 30 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 529 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 2 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
